seo.title: Skeleton — Feedback
seo.description: Documentação do Skeleton: placeholder de carregamento com pulso por opacidade, forma e largura por atributo, decorativo via aria-hidden e com a animação desligada sob movimento reduzido.
seo.aiSummary: O componente Skeleton renderiza um placeholder que imita a caixa do conteúdo que vai substituir. Forma e largura vêm dos atributos data-shape e data-width, o fundo é a cor primária a 10% sobre o container, e o pulso por opacidade é desligado pela própria folha de estilo sob prefers-reduced-motion. O placeholder é decorativo (aria-hidden): quem anuncia o carregamento é a região que o contém, com role status, aria-busy e nome acessível.

anatomy.title: Anatomia
anatomy.item1: Raiz — div com a classe base do esqueleto: fundo suave, cantos arredondados e pulso por opacidade.
anatomy.item2: Forma e largura — data-shape escolhe a forma (linha de texto, título, avatar ou preenchimento) e data-width escolhe a fração da largura do container. A folha de estilo continua dona das medidas.
anatomy.item3: Container — o wrapper externo recebe role="status", aria-busy e aria-label; o esqueleto recebe aria-hidden.

guidelines.title: Guidelines Obrigatórias
guidelines.item1: Use Skeleton quando o tempo de carregamento esperado é maior que 300ms e a estrutura final é conhecida.
guidelines.item2: Replique a caixa do conteúdo final para evitar layout shift quando ele chegar.
guidelines.item3: Aplique aria-hidden="true" no esqueleto e role="status" com aria-busy="true" no container.
guidelines.item4: Não recrie o controle de movimento: a folha de estilo já para o pulso quando o sistema pede prefers-reduced-motion, e forçar a animação por cima quebra WCAG 2.3.3.
guidelines.item5: Para operações com progresso mensurável (upload, download), prefira Progress.

accessibility.title: Acessibilidade
accessibility.summary: Atende WCAG 2.2 AA — 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions), porque o pulso é desligado sob movimento reduzido, e 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value), porque a região que carrega tem papel e nome enquanto o placeholder fica fora da árvore de acessibilidade.

items.item1: Skeleton recebe aria-hidden="true" — leitor de tela ignora o placeholder.
items.item2: O container recebe role="status", aria-busy="true" e aria-label descrevendo o que carrega.
items.item3: O pulso é desligado quando o sistema pede movimento reduzido — a regra vive na folha de estilo do componente, não no consumidor.
items.item4: Após carregar, remova aria-busy do container — leitor anuncia que o conteúdo está pronto.
items.item5: Não use Skeleton como único indicador de loading se a operação dura mais de 10s — adicione texto.

keyboard.title: Navegação por Teclado
keyboard.description: Skeleton é decorativo e não recebe foco. O foco permanece no último elemento interativo até o conteúdo real carregar.

aria.title: Atributos ARIA
aria.ariaHidden: aria-hidden="true" obrigatório no Skeleton (ou no container que o envolve).
aria.ariaBusy: aria-busy="true" no container indica carregamento; ele precisa de role para ser anunciado.
aria.ariaLabel: aria-label no container descreve o conteúdo que carrega (ex: "Carregando lista de pedidos").

screenReader.title: Leitor de Tela
screenReader.loading: Anuncia o aria-label do container junto com "busy" ou "loading".
screenReader.ignored: Não anuncia os Skeletons individualmente — apenas o estado do container.
screenReader.ready: Quando aria-busy passa a false, anuncia o conteúdo real recém-carregado.

progress.name: Progress
progress.description: Para operações com progresso mensurável (upload, download).

aspectRatio.name: AspectRatio
aspectRatio.description: Wrap Skeleton em AspectRatio para placeholders de imagem com proporção.

card.name: Card
card.description: Padrão comum: Skeleton dentro de Card replica a estrutura final.

notes.title: Notas de Implementação
notes.item1: Tempo mínimo: não exiba Skeleton para loading inferior a 300ms — flash visual atrapalha. Use setTimeout antes de mostrar.
notes.item2: Layout shift: dimensões do Skeleton devem aproximar do conteúdo final. Erro comum é Skeleton menor que conteúdo, causando shift ao carregar.
notes.item3: Aninhamento: 2–3 elementos por bloco bastam. Evite reconstruir toda a estrutura final — gera ruído visual.
notes.item4: Movimento reduzido: o pulso já é desligado pela folha de estilo sob prefers-reduced-motion. Não é opcional e não precisa ser repetido no consumidor — é WCAG 2.3.3.
notes.item5: Container aria-busy: alternar para false ao terminar é o que dispara o anúncio de "pronto" pelo leitor de tela.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.description: Skeleton é um componente passivo — não dispara eventos. Para rastrear tempo de carregamento, instrumente o callback que substitui o Skeleton pelo conteúdo real (ex: track('list_loaded', { duration_ms })).

en.title: Skeleton
en.description: Pulsating visual placeholder that mirrors the final content structure while it loads.

seo.title: Skeleton — Feedback
seo.description: Skeleton documentation: loading placeholder with an opacity pulse, shape and width set by attribute, decorative via aria-hidden, and animation switched off under reduced motion.
seo.aiSummary: The Skeleton component renders a placeholder that mirrors the box of the content it will be replaced by. Shape and width come from the data-shape and data-width attributes, the background is the primary colour at 10% over the container, and the opacity pulse is switched off by the stylesheet itself under prefers-reduced-motion. The placeholder is decorative (aria-hidden): the loading state is announced by the region that contains it, with role status, aria-busy and an accessible name.

labels.list: List — 5 items with avatar and text

anatomy.title: Anatomy
anatomy.item1: Root — div with the skeleton base class: soft background, rounded corners, and an opacity pulse.
anatomy.item2: Shape and width — data-shape picks the shape (text line, heading, avatar, or fill) and data-width picks the fraction of the container width. The stylesheet stays the owner of the measurements.
anatomy.item3: Container — the outer wrapper holds role="status", aria-busy, and aria-label; the skeleton holds aria-hidden.

guidelines.title: Mandatory Guidelines
guidelines.item1: Use Skeleton when expected loading time exceeds 300ms and the final structure is known.
guidelines.item2: Mirror the box of the final content to avoid layout shift when it arrives.
guidelines.item3: Apply aria-hidden="true" on the skeleton and role="status" with aria-busy="true" on the container.
guidelines.item4: Do not rebuild the motion control: the stylesheet already stops the pulse when the system asks for prefers-reduced-motion, and forcing the animation back on breaks WCAG 2.3.3.
guidelines.item5: For operations with measurable progress (upload, download), prefer Progress.

dimensions.name: Skeleton box
dimensions.good: Text line at three quarters of the width
dimensions.bad: A tall solid block in place of a line

shape.name: Skeleton shape
shape.bad: A rectangle in place of the round avatar

motionReduce.name: Reduced motion
motionReduce.format: Let the stylesheet switch the pulse off
motionReduce.bad: Animation forced on top of the preference

do.title: Use when
do.item2: Final content structure is known and stable.
do.item3: You want to reduce wait perception with a visual placeholder.
do.item4: Loading multiple items in a list, grid, or card.

dont.title: Do not use when
dont.item1: Loading is very fast (<300ms) — turns into visual noise.
dont.item2: Final content structure is unknown or variable.
dont.item3: There is measurable progress — use Progress with numeric value.
dont.item4: Content is just a short text — a loading sentence is enough.

pair1.do: Skeleton mirroring the final content box — heading, full line, short line.
pair1.dont: A single generic block, which makes the layout jump when the content arrives.

pair2.do: Loading region with a role and a name, and the placeholder hidden from the screen reader.
pair2.dont: Loose skeleton, with no region announcing the load — the screen reader has no idea something is coming.

styles.rectangle: Fills the box the container already establishes — placeholder for images, media, and blocks with a defined ratio.
styles.circle: Circle sized from the size scale — placeholder for avatars and icons.
styles.line: Height derived from the text scale and width as a fraction of the container — placeholder for text lines.

default.label: Default
default.behavior: The skeleton pulses by opacity on a 1.5s cycle; the background is the primary colour at 10% over the container.

motionReduced.label: Reduced Motion
motionReduced.behavior: The stylesheet switches the animation off: the skeleton stays visible and still, with no pulse.

className.description: Extra .nds-* utility classes. Shape and width come from the attributes, not from here.

ariaHidden.description: Already set — the placeholder is noise for screen readers, and the loading state is announced by the container.

rest.description: Accepts any native div attribute (id, data-*, style).

dataShape.description: Placeholder shape. Without it the skeleton has no measurement of its own and depends entirely on the container.

dataWidth.description: Fraction of the container width. Varying width across lines is what makes a block read as a paragraph.

dataSize.description: Avatar measurement on the size scale. Only takes effect on the avatar shape.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.summary: Meets WCAG 2.2 AA — 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions), because the pulse is switched off under reduced motion, and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value), because the loading region has a role and a name while the placeholder stays out of the accessibility tree.

items.item1: Skeleton gets aria-hidden="true" — screen reader ignores the placeholder.
items.item2: The container gets role="status", aria-busy="true", and aria-label describing what is loading.
items.item3: The pulse is switched off when the system asks for reduced motion — the rule lives in the component stylesheet, not in the consumer.
items.item4: After loading, remove aria-busy from the container — screen reader announces content is ready.
items.item5: Do not use Skeleton as the sole loading indicator if the operation lasts longer than 10s — add text.

keyboard.title: Keyboard Navigation
keyboard.description: Skeleton is decorative and does not receive focus. Focus stays on the last interactive element until real content loads.

aria.title: ARIA Attributes
aria.ariaHidden: aria-hidden="true" required on the Skeleton (or the wrapping container).
aria.ariaBusy: aria-busy="true" on the container marks loading; it needs a role to be announced.
aria.ariaLabel: aria-label on the container describes loading content (e.g., "Loading order list").

screenReader.title: Screen Reader
screenReader.loading: Announces the container's aria-label along with "busy" or "loading".
screenReader.ignored: Does not announce individual Skeletons — only the container state.
screenReader.ready: When aria-busy switches to false, announces the freshly loaded real content.

progress.name: Progress
progress.description: For operations with measurable progress (upload, download).

aspectRatio.name: AspectRatio
aspectRatio.description: Wrap Skeleton in AspectRatio for proportional image placeholders.

card.name: Card
card.description: Common pattern: Skeleton inside Card mirrors the final structure.

notes.title: Implementation Notes
notes.item1: Minimum time: do not show Skeleton for loading shorter than 300ms — visual flash hurts. Use setTimeout before showing.
notes.item2: Layout shift: Skeleton dimensions must approximate the final content. Common error is Skeleton smaller than content, shifting layout on load.
notes.item3: Nesting: 2–3 elements per block is enough. Avoid rebuilding the full final structure — visual noise.
notes.item4: Reduced motion: the pulse is already switched off by the stylesheet under prefers-reduced-motion. It is not optional and does not need to be repeated in the consumer — it is WCAG 2.3.3.
notes.item5: Container aria-busy: switching to false on completion is what triggers the "ready" announcement by the screen reader.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.description: Skeleton is a passive component — does not dispatch events. To track loading time, instrument the callback that replaces the Skeleton with real content (e.g., track('list_loaded', { duration_ms })).

functional.title: Functional Behavior
functional.description: What should happen in each state and variant.

item1.result: Opacity pulse, rounded corners, and a background distinct from the container

item2.action: Render with shape and width by attribute
item2.result: The drawn box changes: the avatar comes out square with a round radius, the line takes the requested fraction

item3.action: Render the skeleton inside a loading region
item3.result: The placeholder stays out of the accessibility tree

item4.action: Loading container with role and state
item4.result: The region exposes role status, aria-busy, and an accessible name

item5.result: The skeleton animation is switched off

accessibility.title: Verifiable Accessibility
accessibility.description: Criteria that automated tools should confirm.
accessibility.item1: No violations reported by axe-core in the default state
accessibility.item2: Skeleton with aria-hidden does not appear in the accessibility tree
accessibility.item3: Loading container exposes role status with an accessible name (WCAG 4.1.2)
accessibility.item4: Animation switched off when prefers-reduced-motion is active (WCAG 2.3.3)
accessibility.item5: Placeholder distinguishable from the container background — not a text contrast criterion, but a perceptible luminance difference

accessibility.title: Accesibilidad
accessibility.summary: Cumple WCAG 2.2 AA — 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions), porque el pulso se apaga bajo movimiento reducido, y 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value), porque la región que carga tiene rol y nombre mientras el placeholder queda fuera del árbol de accesibilidad.

items.item1: Skeleton recibe aria-hidden="true" — el lector de pantalla ignora el placeholder.
items.item2: El container recibe role="status", aria-busy="true" y aria-label describiendo lo que carga.
items.item3: El pulso se apaga cuando el sistema pide movimiento reducido — la regla vive en la hoja de estilo del componente, no en el consumidor.
items.item4: Tras cargar, remueve aria-busy del container — el lector anuncia que el contenido está listo.
items.item5: No uses Skeleton como único indicador de loading si la operación dura más de 10s — añade texto.

keyboard.title: Navegación por Teclado
keyboard.description: Skeleton es decorativo y no recibe foco. El foco permanece en el último elemento interactivo hasta que el contenido real cargue.

aria.title: Atributos ARIA
aria.ariaHidden: aria-hidden="true" obligatorio en el Skeleton (o en el container que lo envuelve).
aria.ariaBusy: aria-busy="true" en el container indica carga; necesita role para ser anunciado.
aria.ariaLabel: aria-label en el container describe el contenido que carga (ej.: "Cargando lista de pedidos").

screenReader.title: Lector de Pantalla
screenReader.loading: Anuncia el aria-label del container junto con "busy" o "loading".
screenReader.ignored: No anuncia los Skeletons individualmente — solo el estado del container.
screenReader.ready: Cuando aria-busy pasa a false, anuncia el contenido real recién cargado.

progress.name: Progress
progress.description: Para operaciones con progreso medible (upload, download).

aspectRatio.name: AspectRatio
aspectRatio.description: Wrap Skeleton en AspectRatio para placeholders de imagen con proporción.

card.name: Card
card.description: Patrón común: Skeleton dentro de Card replica la estructura final.

notes.title: Notas de Implementación
notes.item1: Tiempo mínimo: no muestres Skeleton para loading menor a 300ms — el flash visual incomoda. Usa setTimeout antes de mostrar.
notes.item2: Layout shift: las dimensiones del Skeleton deben aproximarse al contenido final. Error común es Skeleton menor que el contenido, causando shift al cargar.
notes.item3: Anidamiento: 2–3 elementos por bloque bastan. Evita reconstruir toda la estructura final — genera ruido visual.
notes.item4: Movimiento reducido: la hoja de estilo ya apaga el pulso bajo prefers-reduced-motion. No es opcional y no hace falta repetirlo en el consumidor — es WCAG 2.3.3.
notes.item5: Container aria-busy: cambiarlo a false al terminar es lo que dispara el anuncio de "listo" del lector de pantalla.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.description: Skeleton es un componente pasivo — no dispara eventos. Para rastrear tiempo de carga, instrumenta el callback que reemplaza el Skeleton por el contenido real (ej.: track('list_loaded', { duration_ms })).

functional.title: Comportamiento Funcional
functional.description: Lo que debe ocurrir en cada estado y variante.

item1.result: Pulso por opacidad, esquinas redondeadas y fondo distinto del container

item2.action: Renderizar con forma y ancho por atributo
item2.result: La caja dibujada cambia: el avatar sale cuadrado con radio circular, la línea ocupa la fracción pedida

item3.action: Renderizar el esqueleto dentro de una región de carga
item3.result: El placeholder queda fuera del árbol de accesibilidad

item4.action: Container de carga con rol y estado
item4.result: La región expone role status, aria-busy y nombre accesible

item5.result: La animación del esqueleto se apaga

accessibility.title: Accesibilidad Verificable
accessibility.description: Criterios que herramientas automatizadas deben confirmar.
accessibility.item1: Sin violaciones reportadas por axe-core en el estado predeterminado
accessibility.item2: Esqueleto con aria-hidden no aparece en el árbol de accesibilidad
accessibility.item3: Container de carga expone role status con nombre accesible (WCAG 4.1.2)
accessibility.item4: Animación apagada cuando prefers-reduced-motion está activo (WCAG 2.3.3)
accessibility.item5: Placeholder distinguible del fondo del container — no es criterio de contraste de texto, sino diferencia de luminancia perceptible
